content: 1. Journals and Publications in Toxicology and Related Fields: The Journal of the Indian Society of Toxicology is published by the Indian Society of Toxicology in Pondicherry, India. The Journal of Occupational and Environmental Hygiene is published by the Taylor and Francis Group in Abingdon-on-Thames, United Kingdom. The Journal of Medical Toxicology is published by Springer in Berlin, Germany. Neurotoxicology is published by Elsevier in Amsterdam, Netherlands. The Scandinavian Journal of Work, Environment and Health is published by the Nordic Association of Occupational Safety and Health in Helsinki, Finland. Toxicology is another journal published by Elsevier in Amsterdam, Netherlands. Toxicology and Applied Pharmacology is published by Academic Press in San Diego, California, USA. Toxicology Letters and Toxicon are both published by Elsevier in Amsterdam, Netherlands. 2. French-Language Journals: Archives des maladies professionnelles de médecine du travail et de sécurité sociale is published by Elsevier in Paris, France. Bulletin d’information toxicologique is published by the Institut national de santé publique du Québec and the Centre antipoison du Québec in Canada. Thérapie is also published by Elsevier in Paris, France. 3. Italian-Language Journals: La Medicina del lavoro is published by Mattioli 1885 srl in Fidenza, Italy. Giornale Italiano di Medicina del Lavoro ed Ergonomia is published by ICS Maugeri in Pavia, Italy. 4. Portuguese-Language Journals: The Revista brasileira de toxicologia, previously published in São Paulo, Brazil, has been replaced by Applied Research in Toxicology. 5. Spanish-Language Journals: Acta Toxicológica Argentina is published by the Portal of Scientific and Technical Publications in Buenos Aires, Argentina. Revista de Toxicología is published by the Asociación Española de Toxicología in Valencia, Spain. Revista de Salud Ambiental is published by the Sociedad Española de Sanidad Ambiental in Madrid, Spain. 6. Online Resources for Toxicology and General Medicine: Numerous online databases and resources provide information on toxicology and general medicine, many of which are free or available at low cost. Examples include poison information databases, chemical hazard portals, and toxicological evaluation platforms. Some resources require registration or subscription, particularly for full access, while others are freely accessible without registration. 7. Structured Toxicovigilance Systems: Brazil: The Brazilian National Health Surveillance Agency (ANVISA) oversees the approval, registration, and supervision of products such as food, cosmetics, pesticides, and pharmaceuticals. Poisoning cases are reported to the national Information System for Notifiable Diseases. The Brazilian Network of Poison Centres comprises 30 centres, which use a unified database, DATATOX, for clinical and epidemiological studies. Canada: The Canadian Surveillance System for Poison Information is a pan-Canadian toxicovigilance system aggregating data from five poison centres. It provides near real-time surveillance and national statistics on poisonings, chemical intoxications, and adverse drug reactions. Health Canada supports this initiative by improving data quality, providing training, and deploying epidemiologists to poison centres. 8. Data Collection and Documentation in Poison Centres: This data is essential for risk assessment, toxicovigilance, and prevention efforts. 9. Examples of Toxicovigilance Systems: Toxicovigilance systems are established in various countries to monitor and respond to poisoning incidents. This detailed explanation provides a comprehensive overview of the journals, resources, and toxicovigilance systems mentioned in the original content.
